accidents: read_head reads seq with int(): a string, a float (truncated), a bool and a non-ASCII digit string all read as a seq (log.py:629-636); an infinite float raises OverflowError out of verify_chain, which read_head does not catch
read_head reads mac with str(): any JSON value is a mac, spelled as Python's str() spells it (log.py:633)

a rekey payload whose extra key holds an integer of more than 4300 digits fails json.loads (CPython's int digit limit), so the row reads as naming no key (payload_invalid) though its fingerprints are well formed (log.py:941)
result: report: verify_chain(conn, keyring, current_fingerprint).to_dict(), with an int outside i64 as {'int': decimal} and a str holding a lone surrogate as {'cps': [...]}; or error: the exception type verify_chain raised
ring: the keys directory: current -> <store_id>.key, each retired [name, key] -> <store_id>.<name>.key, head -> <store_id>.head, origin -> <store_id>.origin; each a hex of the file's bytes, null when there is no such file
rows: the rows the log table holds, in seq order; verify_chain reads those with seq > 0 (iter_rows)
